ModMetaData.name: Grandmaster 21
ModMetaData.author: aRed
ModMetaData.description:
RimWorld skills normally end at 20. This mod adds exactly one more level: 21, Grandmaster.
Level 21 can never be randomly generated. No colonist, raider, trader, refugee, quest pawn, ancient, faction leader or modded super-soldier will ever spawn with it, no matter how many implants, genes, traits or backstory bonuses they have. It must be earned by accumulating an enormous amount of additional experience after a pawn has already reached level 20 - one billion XP by default, configurable in Mod Settings.
Level 21 is the absolute maximum. Level 22 cannot occur.
Newly generated pawns are capped at level 20 unconditionally - there is no setting that relaxes this.
Once earned, level 21 is permanent. It does not decay, and ordinary gameplay cannot take it away - not skill decay, not negative experience, not another mod assigning a lower level, not negative aptitude.
Grandmaster is also the only pawn skill level capable of producing Legendary-quality work. Quality becomes deterministic by skill band, and Inspired Creativity and the Ideology Production Specialist role can no longer push a level-20 pawn to Legendary. Turning deterministic quality off restores vanilla randomness for levels 0-20 but caps them at Masterwork; level 21 is always Legendary. Legendary items from quests, traders, map generation and other non-pawn sources are untouched.
SHOOTING 21 - GRANDMASTER MARKSMAN
The first skill-specific capstone. A Shooting Grandmaster compensates for almost all remaining weapon inaccuracy, ignores cover and ordinary environmental aim penalties, aims and recovers between shots 99% faster, and unlocks per-pawn aim modes: Normal, Killer (aim to kill) and Downed (least-lethal targeting - mobility first, then manipulation, then non-vital extremities, re-aimed after every shot, and firing stops once the target is down). Range, damage, armour and line of sight are untouched - the mastery is the marksman's, not the bullet's. Incompatible with Combat Extended, which disables the marksman package automatically.
MELEE 21 - GRANDMASTER OF COMBAT
The second skill-specific capstone, and a deliberately overpowered one. A Melee Grandmaster controls the immediate battlefield: they strike with near-perfect execution, parry almost anything ordinary melee skill can throw at them, exploit about 99% of the defence an opponent's own skill generates, counterattack instantly when they turn a blow aside, disarm armed foes, land critical strikes from 2x to 10x, cleave through crowded melee, intercept attacks aimed at allies within three tiles, and intercept, deflect and return incoming projectiles - arrows, bullets, grenades and rockets alike.
The Guardian is threat-aware: it does NOT intercept every projectile within three tiles. It reacts only to projectiles that credibly threaten the Grandmaster or a protected ally, so a hundred-round minigun burst that mostly misses produces a handful of reactions rather than a hundred. Hostile fire may be returned to the sender. An ally's accidental friendly fire is instead corrected back toward the enemy it was aimed at, and the ally keeps the shot. A friendly who deliberately force-attacks the Grandmaster with a direct shot is not having an accident, and may find the round coming straight back.
Friendly EXPLOSIVES are handled differently on purpose. An area weapon has no single aim point worth reasoning about, so the Guardian does not try to guess intent: any friendly grenade, rocket or shell that threatens the Grandmaster or a protected ally is treated as a dangerous accident, redirected toward the best available hostile group, or thrown somewhere safe if none is reachable. Protected-pawn safety is a hard constraint, not a preference: a destination that would catch one of your own in the blast, or that the projectile would have to fly through one of them to reach, is rejected outright before anything is weighed. No number of raiders makes a colonist acceptable collateral. It is never sent back at the ally who launched it. The fuse, blast radius and payload all survive - the Guardian decides where it goes off, not whether. Interception never moves the pawn: jobs, pathing and melee engagement are untouched.
Every one of those abilities is driven by the pawn's OWN stats, so no two Grandmasters fight alike. A fast pawn excels at interception and projectile defence. A precise, perceptive one excels at disarming, criticals and returning projectiles to their sender. A physically powerful one excels at cleaving and at hurling deflected explosives absurd distances. A heavily modded pawn becomes correspondingly absurd, and that is intended. A pawn who is downed, unconscious, asleep, stunned, blind or armless loses the abilities that body part was providing.
Armour, weapon damage, damage types and blast radius are untouched: the mastery is the fighter's, not the weapon's. There is no explosion immunity - a successfully redirected doomsday rocket can still kill the Grandmaster who redirected it.
MELEE DODGE: RimWorld caps melee dodge chance at roughly 50% for every pawn, whatever stats feed it. Levels 0-20 stay entirely under that cap - a heavily modded level-20 pawn is still the peak NORMAL combatant. Level 21 is the one level that crosses it, transforming the already-resolved vanilla value into roughly 99.9% effective melee defence. The dodge StatDef itself is never modified, so every other pawn and every other mod reading it are unaffected, and ranged dodge is untouched entirely - a Melee Grandmaster answers projectiles by intercepting them, not by dodging them. A pawn who is downed, unconscious, asleep or stunned gets none of it.
Melee Grandmasters also get their own Normal/Killer/Downed doctrine, separate from the Shooting aim mode. Downed doctrine additionally pulls the blow, stopping short of destroying the limb it is aimed at - something only melee can do.
Incompatible with combat overhauls, which disable the melee package automatically.
CRAFTING 21 - MAGICAL CRAFTSMANSHIP
Research Magical Craftsmanship after Fabrication, build a magical workstation, and choose an eligible existing equipment recipe. A Crafting Grandmaster gathers the real ingredients and one Magical Catalyst, then permanently commits a workstation-owned project. Work can pause and another Crafting Grandmaster can continue it. A normal-speed project takes at least 18 working hours; higher crafting speeds receive diminishing returns.
The result is always vanilla Legendary equipment in its selected material. Its separate craftsmanship has a 50% chance of being Magical, locked once at commitment. Magical currently adds a persistent label, not combat powers. Committed projects cannot be cancelled or refunded. Destroying the workstation loses its project; active workstations cannot be deconstructed or uninstalled.
This is an experimental foundation: catalysts are obtained through Development mode's Spawn thing menu. The feature builds against real RimWorld 1.6 DLLs and has headless checks, but full save/reload and gameplay have not yet been verified in RimWorld.
MEDICINE 21 - GRANDMASTER PHYSICIAN (EXPERIMENTAL)
The miracle is the physician, not the medicine: no research, items, machines or implants are added. A Medicine Grandmaster tends with exact, deterministic quality instead of a random roll, and extracts a meaningfully higher tier from any medicine - discovered from the loaded game, so modded medicine works too (vanilla: herbal 100%, industrial 130%, glitterworld 160%). A condition they actually tend receives Grandmaster Treatment: that specific injury heals faster, or immunity to that specific disease develops faster, while the treatment lasts. Their surgery never takes a failure outcome, though every requirement of the operation still applies.
A Grandmaster Medicine command (left-click to choose, right-click to act) adds three personal interventions, each performed as a medical job that costs ordinary medicine and hours of the Grandmaster's work - no cooldowns: Cure one pathological condition (diseases, chronic illness, food poisoning - never wounds, missing parts, implants or unknown states), Reconstruct one missing natural body part that has not been replaced, and Resuscitate a pawn while the body is still biologically recoverable (judged by its decay: hours unpreserved, longer refrigerated, indefinitely frozen). Resuscitation rebuilds only the vital organs life requires, leaves lost limbs lost, turns the worst of the death trauma into permanent scars, leaves the pawn unconscious in resuscitation shock for six hours, and never works on a destroyed brain; a revived enemy stays an enemy.
Medicine 21 builds against the real RimWorld 1.6 assemblies and has headless checks, but has NOT yet been verified in a running game. Tuning numbers are provisional.
Other skills do not have Level 21 abilities yet.
Before removing this mod, remove all magical workstations and catalysts from your save, then use "Prepare Save for Uninstall" at the bottom of Mod Settings. That action reduces every level 21 skill to 20, clears stored Grandmaster progression, and removes Medicine 21 treatments, modes, resuscitation shock and interventions in progress; it does not remove crafting objects or artifact metadata. Destroying active workstations loses their projects. Then save, exit, disable the mod and reload the cleaned save. Keep a backup: the full remove-and-reload sequence has not yet been verified in gameplay testing.
Incompatible with mods that also remove or replace the skill cap, such as unlimited-skill mods.
